label_conventions: Whitney collection pages list fields in this order: artist, title, date, medium, dimensions, accession number, edition (only if the work is an edition), credit line, rights line. Each value sits under a bold field name (Date, Medium, Dimensions, Accession number, Edition, Credit line, Rights and reproductions).

Whitney credit lines for acquisitions start with 'Purchase, with funds from the [Committee]' (Drawing and Print Committee, Film and Video Committee, Painting and Sculpture Committee). They can add named donors: 'Purchase, with funds from the Film and Video Committee and Robert Rosenkranz'. A bequest reads 'Josephine N. Hopper Bequest, by exchange'.
Whitney edition line is separate and uses a pipe: '1/5 | 2 APs' or 'HC | Ed. 5, 2 APs'. The line says AP in the plural ('2 APs'), not '+ 2 AP'.

Whitney video medium is one comma chain: type, colour mode, sound, run time, then extra materials after 'with': 'Video installation, color, sound, 67 min., with ribbons, mattresses, pillows, sheets, and custom flooring'. Multi-screen works say 'Four-channel video installation, black-and-white and color, sound, 14 min. looped'.

Whitney dimensions use inches first with cm in brackets and a part prefix: 'Sheet: 22 1/8 × 30 in. (56.2 × 76.2 cm)', 'Overall: 89 5/8 × 74 1/4 in. (227.6 × 188.6 cm)'. Installations say only 'Dimensions variable'. Fractions use 1/8 style, and × is the multiplication sign.

Whitney medium for an unspecific textile is a single word ('Fabric'); drawings say 'Graphite on paper'. Whitney rights line is '© Artist' or '© artist or artist's estate', and may add 'courtesy of [gallery]' ('© Stanley Whitney, courtesy of Lisson Gallery').

MoMA collection pages put title, year and medium in the header, then fields Medium, Dimensions (or Duration for time-based work), Credit, Object number, Copyright. MoMA medium for painting: 'Acrylic and graphite on canvas, two panels'. Support list goes material to material and ends with a panel or part count.

MoMA dimensions put inches first with the inch mark " and cm in brackets, with a part prefix: 'Each panel: 97 × 60" (246.4 × 152.4 cm)'. Time-based work uses a Duration field in 'mm:ss min.' form: 'Duration: 12:50 min.'. MoMA video medium is short: 'Video (color, sound)'.

MoMA credit lines: 'Acquired through the generosity of [list of named funds and couples]' (the list runs long and uses 'and' before the last name), 'Gift of [name]', or just a fund name ('Fund for the Twenty-First Century'). MoMA object numbers have the form 'sequence.year' ('632.2013', '757.2022', '255.2021.a-b' for parts).

MoMA media/digital works can use a materials-style medium: 'Custom hardware and software (color, sound, generative algorithm with artificial intelligence)' with 'Dimensions variable'. Copyright line can carry the gallery: '© 2026 Suzanne Jackson. Courtesy of the Artist and Ortuzar Projects, New York.' MoMA also publishes a separate 'Gallery label' text paragraph, after the metadata, dated by exhibition.

Tate collection credit lines start with 'Tate.' then the acquisition verb in the past tense with a year at the end: 'Tate. Purchased with funds provided by the Acquisitions Fund for African Art supported by Guaranty Trust Bank Plc 2014'. The year is the acquisition year with no comma. Tate dimensions use cm and often list each panel ('Two panels 212 × 212.3 cm, 212 × 212.9 cm'). Tate medium uses UK spelling and 'on' ('Acrylic, transfers, coloured pencil and charcoal on paper').

Tate acquisition press lists give artist (b.YEAR) or (YEAR–YEAR), then the title in italics and year on the same line, then medium, then 'Dimensions: ... mm' (mm, not cm, in the press list), then 'Acquired from [Gallery]' or '(Gallery, Frieze London)'. Installations say 'Dimensions variable'. Video medium reads 'Video, high definition, projection, colour and sound' with the run time on its own line: 'Duration: 25 min'. A work with a title in two languages puts the second language on its own line under the title (Espíritu de Camala).

Tate 2025 press list adds birth place and residence inside the artist bracket: '(b. Dodoma, Tanzania, 1964; lives and works in London)'. The 2023 list uses only '(b.1991)' with no space after 'b.'. Tate artist names can carry honours ('Lubaina Himid CBE RA'). Tate artwork pages list the date with an en dash for ranges ('1997–9', '2017–18', shortened second year).

Venice Biennale (Arte 2024) artist page header gives place and base only, no birth year, for a collective: 'Founded in Paris, France, 2004' then 'Based in Palermo, Italy'. Venice 2026 artist list uses 'Born YEAR, City, Country. Lives in City, Country' and 'Founded YEAR, City, Country' for collectives and organisations. Deceased artists end with 'D. YEAR' (Born 1945, Dakar, Senegal. D. 2017). Duos list two sets of Born/Lives clauses split by a semicolon. Multiple residences join with 'and' or semicolons ('Lives in Beirut, Lebanon and Paris, France').

Serpentine captions run as one paragraph: 'Artist, Title, date. Medium. Dimensions variable. Commissioned by X. Courtesy of the artist and Gallery A, City, City and City, Gallery B, City and Gallery C, City. Photographer: Name. © Artist'. Year ranges use a hyphen ('2022-23'). 'Commissioned by' comes before 'Courtesy'. Gallery locations list every city after the gallery name. Serpentine artist bios use '(b. 1962, London, United Kingdom)' and add '; lives and works in New Mexico, USA' only sometimes. Dimensions are inches first, cm in brackets when the work is a US work ('65 x 389 in. (165.1 x 988.06 cm)').

Gwangju Biennale captions use a fixed chain of sentences: 'Artist, Title, year. Medium list. Dimensions variable, N minutes. Courtesy of the artist [and Gallery]. Commissioned by the 15th Gwangju Biennale. Courtesy of the Gwangju Biennale Foundation.' Medium lists are full material lists in lower case after the first word (Hand dyed upcycled silk organza, acrylic vessel (containing: ...)). A bracket inside the medium holds the list of living material. Duration sits on the dimensions line ('Dimensions variable, 10 minutes').

Berlin Biennale (13th) caption lists several works in one caption, each bold artist name then italic title, year, then © line, then collection or gallery after a semicolon ('© VG Bild-Kunst, Bonn 2025; Sammlung Berlinische Galerie – Landesmuseum ...'). 'Courtesy' is used for living artists' lenders ('Courtesy Everybody Needs Art; Longtermhandstand, Budapest'). Hidden or withheld work gets '(work in hiding)' in place of an image credit. Berlin bios use an asterisk for birth ('*1933 in Kraubath an der Mur, Austria–2013 in Vienna, Austria') and the fields 'Places of belonging:', 'Affinity:', 'Book:'. There is no 'lives and works' line.

documenta fifteen captions start with 'documenta fifteen:' then collective or artist, italic title, year, work type or view ('installation view', 'Performance'), venue, city, full date (month day, year), then 'photo: Name'. Venue codes appear (WH22, Hübner areal). Collectives are listed with a pipe ('Atis Rezistans | Ghetto Biennale') or 'and' ('Cinema Caravan and Takashi Kuribayashi'). There is no medium or dimension line in the documenta fifteen captions seen; a work with no title takes the activity as title.
Hayward Gallery Touring captions are short: 'Artist, Title (detail), year. © Artist. Courtesy of Gallery, City and City.' No medium or dimensions appear in the caption.

Sharjah Biennial 16 participant list uses an asterisk after the name for 'Participants presenting new commissions'. Collectives list members in brackets; collaborations use 'with' ('Betty Adii with Septina Layan'). The 'Commissioned by Sharjah Art Foundation' credit appears on Sharjah-origin works shown elsewhere (as in the Serpentine caption).

Courtesy formula: 'Courtesy of the artist and [Gallery], [City]' (Serpentine, Gwangju) or 'Courtesy the artist, [Gallery], and [Institution]' (ARTnews/Venice, no 'of') or 'Courtesy [Gallery]' alone (no artist) for estates and lenders ('Courtesy Galerie Cécile Fakhoury'). Multiple galleries are joined with commas and a final 'and', and each gets its cities, e.g. 'Lehmann Maupin, New York, Seoul, and London'. Photo credit may come before courtesy, joined with a slash ('Photo Studio Kukla/Courtesy the artist and ...').

Order of the credit block in biennial captions: (1) medium, (2) dimensions or duration, (3) 'Commissioned by' or 'Produced with the support of', (4) 'Courtesy of', (5) photo credit, (6) copyright symbol. Museums with collections put the credit line (Purchase/Gift/Acquired) before the copyright line and after dimensions and accession number.

Terms for time and size: 'Dimensions variable' stays after a period or comma and is never given a unit. Run time forms vary by institution: '67 min.' (Whitney), '12:50 min.' (MoMA), 'Duration: 25 min' (Tate), '10 minutes' (Gwangju). Colour spelling follows the institution: US 'color' (Whitney, MoMA) and UK 'colour' (Tate).

Edition forms seen: '1/5 | 2 APs' and 'HC | Ed. 5, 2 APs' (Whitney). No institution in the sources printed 'Edition 2/3 + 2 AP' on its public page; that form is common in gallery checklists but was not verified here.

Date forms: single year ('1998'), range with en dash and full second year ('2021–2023', MoMA, Berlin 2015–2017), hyphen in Serpentine ('2022-23'), slash for reworked photographs/editions ('1989/ 2023' in the Tate list), 'Original von 1945' for re-created works (Berlin), and '(detail)' after the title when an image is a crop.

Not found on a public page: Venice Biennale per-artwork wall-label wording, documenta 16 (2027) labels, and New Museum or Hayward Gallery per-artwork labels. The New Museum site returns an empty page without JavaScript. Hayward and Southbank Centre pages return HTTP 403. Tate artwork pages (tate.org.uk/art/artworks/...) returned no credit line text in the HTML received, so the Tate rules above come from a Tate shop product page and Tate press releases.
